change.title: stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields

source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses stripe-node 14.22.0 with apiVersion pinned to 2023-10-16 in libs/stripe.ts, so none of these changes break production today. Stripe keeps old pinned versions working. The SDK is nine majors behind, though, and the only upgrade path is one coherent move: bump stripe to 23.x and move the pinned API version to 2026-09-30.endive. That bundles the node 19–23 majors and the Dahlia/Endive API versions. Endive-only field changes the repo may hit belong in the same PR. Checkout payment_method_types is likely present in an uncaptured create-checkout-session route; ui_mode only matters if set explicitly. The migration agent should check several things. First, that libs/stripe.ts uses `new Stripe(...)`. Second, subscription period fields read in libs/supabaseAdmin.ts after the retrieve (Basil moved current_period_* to items). Third, any decimal price fields typed as Stripe.Decimal. Fourth, any checkout/portal session routes not in the scan, for payment_method_types and ui_mode. Finally, the webhook endpoint's API version in the Stripe dashboard must match the new pin.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23.0.0 pins 2026-09-30.endive. Bumping the SDK and moving the apiVersion string in libs/stripe.ts from 2023-10-16 to endive is this one move.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-03-25-dahlia-api-version (api-version): API major 2026-03-25.dahlia with breaking changes (Checkout ui_mode enum values, events_from on event destinations, Capabilities risk requirements, Stripe.js method removals), effective 2026-03-25. Going from 2023-10-16 to endive passes through Dahlia, so its server-side breaking changes are absorbed by the same bump.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "As the first version in the Dahlia release, `2026-03-25.dahlia` introduces both breaking changes and new features"
- stripe:node-22-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed, effective 2026-04-02. This is an intermediate major between 14.22.0 and 23. The client must be built with `new Stripe(...)`, the reworked types must be adopted, and no per-request host override may be used. These edits are part of the same SDK bump.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:"
- stripe:node-21-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 21.0.0: pins 2026-03-25.dahlia, drops Node 16, decimal_string fields become Stripe.Decimal, wrong webhook parsing method throws, effective 2026-03-25. This is an intermediate major. Its changes are: Dahlia pin, decimal_string fields typed as Stripe.Decimal (check any unit_amount_decimal handling in the price upsert), and a throw when the wrong webhook parsing method is used. The repo uses constructEvent, which is the correct method for snapshot events. All of it is handled within the same SDK bump.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "All `decimal_string` fields changed type from `string` to `Stripe.Decimal` in both request params and response objects."
- stripe:node-20-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 20.0.0: pins 2025-11-17.clover; v2 array params use indexed serialization (may break mock-server tests), effective 2025-11-18. This is an intermediate major (Clover pin; v2 array serialization only affects mock-server tests). It is absorbed by the same SDK bump.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "This may break any unit tests that expect the latter behavior when setting up a mock server."
- stripe:node-19-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 19.0.0: pins 2025-09-30.clover; parseThinEvent renamed parseEventNotification, v2 delete returns V2DeletedObject, v2 nullable props optional; 19.x deprecated (Files API timeout bug), effective 2025-09-30. This is an intermediate major (Clover pin; parseThinEvent rename, which the repo does not use). It is absorbed by the same SDK bump.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Rename function `StripeClient.parseThinEvent` to `StripeClient.parseEventNotification` and remove the `Stripe.ThinEvent` interface."
- stripe:2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout (field-removed): payment_method_types removed from Checkout Sessions create, and paymentMethodTypes option removed from Elements deferred intents (Stripe.js), effective 2026-09-30. This only bites once the API version is endive. Supabase/Stripe starter code of this shape usually creates Checkout Sessions with payment_method_types: ['card'] in a create-checkout-session route the scan did not capture. Once on endive that returns a 400, so it must be removed in the same PR.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "We [removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Sessions]"
- stripe:2026-03-25-checkout-ui-mode-enum (field-renamed): Checkout Session ui_mode enum values updated (Checkout Sessions and Payment Links), effective 2026-03-25. This only applies after the API bump. If the (uncaptured) checkout session creation sets ui_mode explicitly, the value must be mapped to the new enum in the same PR. If ui_mode is unset, nothing changes.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "Updates Checkout Session UI mode enum values"

callSites.why: It pins apiVersion '2023-10-16' and constructs the client. Both the version string and the constructor form (new Stripe) must change with the SDK major.
webhooks.constructEvent and the event payload shapes the handler reads change with the API version that the new SDK pins. Webhook endpoint versions must stay aligned.
subscriptions.retrieve with expand: on newer API versions (Basil and later), current_period_start/end moved to subscription items. Any reads of those fields when upserting subscriptions will break.
customers.create typings and params change across stripe-node majors 15–23. Recompile and verify.
customers.update (name, phone) typings change across the SDK majors. Recompile and verify.

record.prBody:
## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Bumped stripe 14.22.0 to 23.0.0 using npm, and set apiVersion to 2026-09-30.endive in libs/stripe.ts. The subscription period start and end are now read from subscriptions.items.data[0] in libs/supabaseAdmin.ts. I loosened some types to fit the v23 typings. Price.type and Price.interval in types.ts are now literal unions, with casts in upsertPriceRecord. UserDetails.payment_method is now `any`, and the payment_method[type] lookup is cast. The repo uses neither constructEventWithoutVerification nor ErrorType, and constructEvent is unchanged. I found no checkout-session route, so there is no payment_method_types or ui_mode to change. Typecheck and build pass. I added test/stripe23.test.mjs, which checks the installed version, the endive pin and the item-level period read.

Files touched:
- `libs/stripe.ts`
- `libs/supabaseAdmin.ts`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `test/stripe23.test.mjs`
- `types.ts`

### Why

stripe-node 23 pins the endive API version, and its types removed Subscription.current_period_* (moved to items since Basil). Its types also changed Price and PaymentMethod typings, so the old code no longer compiled.

> Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| stripe23 | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- stripe23, added by the agent: `export NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL='https://placeholder.supabase.co' NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY='placeholder' SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY='placeholder' STRIPE_SECRET_KEY='placeholder' NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY='placeholder' STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET='placeholder' NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node test/stripe23.test.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL.

Test of this change: `stripe23`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Endive response shapes were not exercised against the live API.
- The Stripe dashboard webhook endpoint's API version must be set to 2026-09-30.endive.
- The deploy runtime must be Node 20 or later.
- The proof test is a source and version check, not a runtime test.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Subscription current_period_start and current_period_end now come from the first subscription item. This assumes single-item subscriptions.
- The API version is pinned to 2026-09-30.endive, so webhook payloads and responses use endive shapes.

---

## Result
Files changed: libs/stripe.ts, libs/supabaseAdmin.ts, package-lock.json, package.json, test/stripe23.test.mjs, types.ts
Verdict: migrated. Bumped stripe 14.22.0 to 23.0.0 using npm, and set apiVersion to 2026-09-30.endive in libs/stripe.ts. The subscription period start and end are now read from subscriptions.items.data[0] in libs/supabaseAdmin.ts. I loosened some types to fit the v23 typings. Price.type and Price.interval in types.ts are now literal unions, with casts in upsertPriceRecord. UserDetails.payment_method is now `any`, and the payment_method[type] lookup is cast. The repo uses neither constructEventWithoutVerification nor ErrorType, and constructEvent is unchanged. I found no checkout-session route, so there is no payment_method_types or ui_mode to change. Typecheck and build pass. I added test/stripe23.test.mjs, which checks the installed version, the endive pin and the item-level period read.
Unproven: Endive response shapes were not exercised against the live API.; The Stripe dashboard webhook endpoint's API version must be set to 2026-09-30.endive.; The deploy runtime must be Node 20 or later.; The proof test is a source and version check, not a runtime test.

preparation.reasoning: No codegen, postinstall, or workspace builds are needed: the scripts are plain next dev/build/start/lint and the supabase CLI is only a devDependency. Supabase and Stripe clients are created at module load or build time, so placeholder env vars keep the build from throwing.

review.summary: The quoted removal (`constructEventWithoutVerification`) does not touch this repo; `app/api/webhooks/route.ts:33` uses `webhooks.constructEvent`, which still typechecks. The real impact of this PR is two jumps at once: stripe-node 14 → 23 and the pinned API version `2023-10-16` → `2026-09-30.endive`. That spans several breaking API releases. The diff fixes the one break the compiler caught (`current_period_start`/`end` moving to subscription items), but it also weakens types with casts and `any`, and nothing exercises runtime behaviour. The checks are typecheck, build and a grep-style test. None of them makes a live Stripe call or replays a webhook, so the `verified` grade overstates what was proven. I'd treat this as needs-review.

concerns.issue: `apiVersion` moves from `2023-10-16` to `2026-09-30.endive`. That changes response shapes and behaviour for every call: `customers.create`, `customers.update` and `subscriptions.retrieve` with `expand: ['default_payment_method']`. It also affects any checkout or portal routes not named here. I couldn't confirm the `endive` version string from memory. It passes typecheck, so it should be in the SDK's `ApiVersion` type in `node_modules/stripe/types`; check that and the quoted CHANGELOG. None of these calls were exercised against Stripe.

Webhook payloads are rendered in the API version configured on the Stripe webhook endpoint, not the SDK's pinned version. The product and price handlers consume `event.data.object` directly. They are now typed against 2026 shapes while possibly receiving older payloads, or the reverse if the endpoint is upgraded. The subscription path is safer because it re-retrieves through the SDK. No test replays a signed webhook.

`subscription.items.data[0].current_period_start/end` assumes a first item always exists; it will throw if `items.data` is empty. It also takes period data from the first item only, which matters if multi-item subscriptions are ever used. Behaviour is equivalent for this app's single-price subscriptions, but this is the main semantic change and it is only grep-tested.

The casts `price.type as Price['type']`, `price.recurring?.interval as Price['interval']` and `(payment_method as any)[payment_method.type]` silence the compiler instead of mapping types. If Stripe 23 widened these unions (for example a new interval or price type), bad values will flow into Supabase unchecked.

`UserDetails.payment_method` becomes `any`, and the `Price` `type`/`interval` fields become hand-written literal unions. Type safety is lost for UI consumers, and the unions can drift from Stripe's. This goes beyond what the API change forces.

stripe 23 declares `engines.node >= 20`, up from >=12. The deployment runtime (Vercel or another host) must run Node 20+. The lockfile also drops `qs` and marks several transitive packages as dev-only; confirm nothing else depended on `qs` at runtime.

The test only checks the installed version and string presence in source files; it proves nothing about runtime behaviour. Other Stripe call sites likely exist (for example checkout-session and portal-link routes in a typical spotify-clone). Those were not named by the match agent and are not covered by any check. Parameters such as `subscription_data.trial_from_plan` may have changed behaviour across these API versions even though they still typecheck.

checkFirst: Grep the repo for every other `stripe.` call (create-checkout-session, create-portal-link, etc.) and review their params against the 2026-09-30 API changelog, not just types.
Confirm `2026-09-30.endive` is listed in stripe-node 23's ApiVersion type and decide whether the Stripe webhook endpoint's API version should be upgraded together with the SDK pin.

Run a test-mode end-to-end flow: checkout, then `customer.subscription.created`, then `subscriptions.retrieve`, then the Supabase upsert. Verify that `current_period_start`/`end` and `default_payment_method` are populated correctly.
Replay signed product, price and subscription webhooks with the Stripe CLI against the new build.
Verify the deployment runtime is Node 20+.

matchReasoning:
Emmah-oo/spotify-clone:stripe:node-23-0-0: The repo uses stripe-node 14.22.0 with apiVersion pinned to 2023-10-16 in libs/stripe.ts, so none of these changes break production today. Stripe keeps old pinned versions working. The SDK is nine majors behind, though, and the only upgrade path is one coherent move: bump stripe to 23.x and move the pinned API version to 2026-09-30.endive. That bundles the node 19–23 majors and the Dahlia/Endive API versions. Endive-only field changes the repo may hit belong in the same PR. Checkout payment_method_types is likely present in an uncaptured create-checkout-session route; ui_mode only matters if set explicitly. The migration agent should check several things. First, that libs/stripe.ts uses `new Stripe(...)`. Second, subscription period fields read in libs/supabaseAdmin.ts after the retrieve (Basil moved current_period_* to items). Third, any decimal price fields typed as Stripe.Decimal. Fourth, any checkout/portal session routes not in the scan, for payment_method_types and ui_mode. Finally, the webhook endpoint's API version in the Stripe dashboard must match the new pin.
